body_ar:
الخضر الراجح فيه أنه نبي من أنبياء بني إسرائيل و أن أنبياء الله قد ختموا بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم و لم يبق أحد منهم حيا بعد النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم قطعا إلا عيسى بن مريم الذي سينزل مجددا لملة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم و من أتباعه و لن ينزل بصفة الرسالة بل سيكسر الصليب و يقتل الخنزير و يحارب النصارى و لذلك فالخضر ما هو إلا مثل غيره من أنبياء بني إسرائيل قد مات مثل ما مات موسى و هارون و غيرهما من أنبياء بني إسرائيل عليهم السلام أجمعين و من أدلة ذلك ما استدل به البخاري في الصحيح على هذا بحديث بن عمر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نظر إليهم ذات ليلة فقال:« أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه فإنه لا يبقى على وجه الأرض ذو نفس منفوسة ممن هو عليها بعد مائة سنة منها»

فكل الذين عاشوا في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ماتوا قبل تمام مائة سنة و آخرهم موتا أبو الطفيل عامر ابن واثلة رضي الله عنه و قد مات سنة مائة من الهجرة و تلك الليلة ليست أول الهجرة فمعناه أنه بقي بعد تلك الليلة سنوات لم يبق فيها أحد من الصحابة و لم يبق فيها أحد من الذين كانوا على وجه الأرض إذ ذاك و لهذا استدل كثير من المحدثين على كذب الذين يدعون التعمير الذين ادعوا أنهم عمروا ثلاث مائة سنة أو أكثر استدل المحدثون على كذبهم بهذا الحديث و كذلك قال الحافظ بن حجر رحمه الله في ترجمة صالح بن كيسان رحمه الله و صالح بن كيسان من كبار أصحاب الزهري من طبقة مالك و معمر بن راشد و عبيد الله بن عمر العمري و غيرهما قال: إن الناس يزعمون أن صالح بن كيسان عاش مائة و ستين سنة و لو كان كذلك لكان قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه و سلم و لو كان كذلك لمات قبل مائة سنة من تلك الليلة.

-----------------------------------------------------------

هل اقترب ظهور الدجال؟

بالنسبة للاقتراب لا يشك فيه فهذه الأمة وهي أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم آخر أمم الدنيا، والدجال خارج فيها لا محالة، ونحن أيضا في آخر قرون هذه الأمة، فلذلك نحن ننتظر الدجال، ولكن لا يخرج الدجال إلا بعد أن تقوم الخلافة الراشدة، وبعد أن يفتح بيت المقدس وتفتح روما، وإذا فتحت روما فسيخرج الدجال، فيخرج خلة بين الشام والعراق فعاث يمينا وعاث شمالا.

-----------------------------------------------------------

هل الذي ليس سلفي العقيدة مشرك؟

لا لأن المقصود هنا في الاعتقاد أن يكون الإنسان مؤمنا بالله وملائكته و كتبه و رسله و اليوم الآخر و القدر خيره و شره فمن كان مؤمنا بهذه فهو المسلم و من كان كافرا بأحد هذه فليس بمسلم فإذا هذا هو الفرق بين المسلم و الكافر هو هذه الأمور الستة و من لا يعلم من العقيدة إلا هذه الأمور الستة ناج يوم القيامة من لم يكن يعلم أي شيء إلا أنه يؤمن بالله و يؤمن بالملائكة و يؤمن بالكتب المنزلة و يؤمن بالرسل إجمالا لا تفصيلا و يؤمن كذلك باليوم الآخر إجمالا لا تفصيلا و يؤمن بالقدر خيره و شره هذا مؤمن قطعا لو مات على هذا دخل الجنة.
body_en:
The preponderant view concerning al-Khidr is that he was a prophet from among the prophets of the Children of Israel; and that the prophets of God were sealed with Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him; and that none of them remained alive after the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him — definitively — except Jesus son of Mary, who will descend as a renewer of the religion of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and as one of his followers. He will not descend in the capacity of messengership; rather he will break the cross and kill the swine and make war on the Christians. Therefore al-Khidr is nothing but like the rest of the prophets of the Children of Israel: he has died, just as Moses died, and Aaron, and others of the prophets of the Children of Israel, peace be upon them all.

Among the evidences for that is what al-Bukhari adduced in the Sahih for this, with the hadith of Ibn ʿUmar, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, looked at them one night and said: 'Do you see this night of yours? At the end of a hundred years from it, there will not remain upon the face of the earth a single breathing soul of those who are upon it.'

All those who lived in the lifetime of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, died before the completion of a hundred years, and the last of them to die was Abu al-Tufayl ʿAmir ibn Wathilah, God be pleased with him, who died in the year one hundred of the Hijra. And that night was not at the beginning of the Hijra, so it means that years remained after that night in which not one of the Companions was left, and in which not one was left of those who had been upon the face of the earth at that time. For this reason many of the hadith scholars have adduced this as evidence for the falsehood of those who claim great longevity — those who claimed that they had lived three hundred years or more; the hadith scholars adduced this hadith as evidence of their lying. Likewise the Hafiz Ibn Hajar, God have mercy on him, said, in his notice on Salih ibn Kaysan, God have mercy on him — and Salih ibn Kaysan is among the senior companions of al-Zuhri, of the generation of Malik and Maʿmar ibn Rashid and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-ʿUmari and others — he said: people claim that Salih ibn Kaysan lived a hundred and sixty years; and if that were so he would have met the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him; and if that were so he would have died before a hundred years from that night.

-----------------------------------------------------------

Has the appearance of the Antichrist drawn near?

As for its drawing near, there is no doubt of it. This community, the community of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, is the last of the communities of this world, and the Antichrist will inevitably come out among it; and we too are in the last of the generations of this community. For that reason we are awaiting the Antichrist. But the Antichrist will not come out until after the rightly guided caliphate arises, and after Jerusalem is conquered and Rome is conquered. When Rome is conquered, the Antichrist will come out. He comes out from a tract between Syria and Iraq, and he wreaked havoc to the right and wreaked havoc to the left.

-----------------------------------------------------------

Is someone who is not Salafi in creed an associator of partners with God?

No. Because what is meant here in the matter of belief is that a person believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the divine decree (al-qadar), its good and its evil. Whoever believes in these is a Muslim, and whoever disbelieves in any one of them is not a Muslim. So this is the difference between the Muslim and the disbeliever: these six matters. And whoever knows nothing of creed (ʿaqīdah) beyond these six matters is saved on the Day of Resurrection. Someone who knew nothing whatever except that he believes in God, and believes in the angels, and believes in the revealed books, and believes in the messengers in a general way and not in detail, and likewise believes in the Last Day in a general way and not in detail, and believes in the divine decree, its good and its evil — this person is a believer beyond question. If he died upon this, he would enter the Garden.

flags.context: the description of what Jesus will do on his descent
options: and make war on the Christians
and do battle with those who worship the cross
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW. The clause is part of an eschatological narration, given without attribution or grading, and the Sheikh adds nothing of his own to it. In English, naming a living religious community as the object of future warfare carries clear reputational risk when read outside that genre. Note that the parallel passage in record 562 of this slice, describing the same event, has 'fight the Jews' at this point and not 'the Christians' — the Sheikh varies the reports he is drawing on. Translated faithfully, neither softened nor strengthened; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: و لو كان كذلك لكان قد أدرك النبي … و لو كان كذلك لمات قبل مائة سنة من تلك الليلة
flags.context: the closing argument from Ibn Hajar
options: render as the source has it and flag that the inference does not follow as printed
flags.note: THE ARGUMENT DOES NOT CLOSE AS PRINTED. The reasoning is meant to be a reductio: if Salih ibn Kaysan had lived 160 years he would have been alive in the Prophet's lifetime, and therefore — by the hadith just quoted — he must have died within a hundred years of that night, which contradicts the claim. As printed, the final clause states the conclusion without the contradiction being drawn, so an English reader cannot see why it refutes anything. A step has probably dropped out in transcription. Nothing has been supplied; the English reproduces the argument as it stands and the gap is flagged.

flags.arabic: الخضر الراجح فيه أنه نبي … قد مات
options: the preponderant view concerning him is that …
flags.note: al-rājiḥ is the language of weighing, not of certainty: the Sheikh presents the view that al-Khidr was a prophet as the preponderant one, and this is a question on which scholars have long differed. Note that he then uses qaṭʿan, 'definitively', for a different and narrower claim — that no prophet remained alive after Muhammad except Jesus. The two levels of certainty are deliberate and must not be levelled in English.

'Those who claim great longevity' renders alladhīna yaddaʿūna al-taʿmīr, a recognised category in the hadith-criticism literature for impostors claiming to have lived for centuries — which is the link back to the question about al-Khidr.
The second section repeats, almost word for word, a passage that also appears in record 562 of this slice; the two are not identical and have both been translated in full.
